## Routing Decisions — Chapter 5B — IMF 2022 Article IV (MAC-010)

---

### U0071 — page 71 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.3, 5B.9 |
| **Lenses cited** | 3, 9 |
| **Relevance** | Documents Banxico's monetary policy response to inflation (rate spread widened to over 6% vs. U.S.), directly characterizing the central bank's rule-based reaction to an inflation shock — evidence of credible monetary rule administration under 5B.3 and timely targeted measure under 5B.9. Documents peso stability mechanism through carry trades and policy framework. |
| **Adjacent context** | U0072 (pension fund market role) is necessary to complete the domestic investor substitution picture — needed to understand whether the monetary rule was effective given portfolio outflows, but U0072 independently meets the evidence test on its own pension-fund stabilization finding and is included separately. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0072 — page 72 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.3, 5B.9 |
| **Lenses cited** | 3, 9 |
| **Relevance** | Quantifies pension fund scale and expected stabilization role: estimated annual purchases of USD 7–10 billion in domestic government securities could match the highest foreigner sales in the last decade. Banxico projection that pension funds could grow from 20% of GDP (2020) to 35–56% of GDP by 2040. Provides measured distributional market-capacity evidence relevant to whether financial markets were structurally resilient under the monetary/fiscal rule framework. |
| **Adjacent context** | None required; this chunk independently meets the evidence test. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0073 — page 73 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| **Lenses cited** | 8, 9 |
| **Relevance** | Contains material distributional evidence: poverty rates by urban/rural (CONEVAL), changes in urban poverty 2018–2020 (36.8% → 40.1%), extreme poverty food basket cost increases for both rural and urban households. Establishes the distributional baseline for evaluating the government's anti-inflation shock response. Annex intro (paragraph 1) is generic framing but the poverty statistics and the food basket cost data are concrete measured outcomes meeting the evidence test independently. |
| **Adjacent context** | Annex header and intro paragraph (sentence 1) are identifying context only; poverty statistics and cost-of-basket figures independently meet the evidence test and are included on that basis. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0074 — page 74 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| **Lenses cited** | 3, 8, 9 |
| **Relevance** | Contains quantitative policy costing for the PACIC anti-inflation package: total MEX$541,223 million (1.86% of GDP) across multiple programs with line-item budget costs. Fuel subsidy alone MEX$395,400 million (1.36% of GDP). Oil revenue windfall offset estimate (MEX$397.8 billion) compared against fuel subsidy cost — provides fiscal-rule evidence under 5B.3 and distributional targeting evidence under 5B.9. |
| **Adjacent context** | None required; the budget table and subsidy-to-revenue offset calculation independently meet the evidence test. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0075 — page 75 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| **Lenses cited** | 3, 6, 8, 9 |
| **Relevance** | Quantified effectiveness of fuel subsidy in containing inflation: subsidies reduced retail prices by up to 30% in June, directly reducing headline inflation by ~2 percentage points (counterfactual peak ~10%). Subsequent decline to 0.2% as fuel prices fell — evidence of monitored and adjusting response. Documents the 2019 shadow-pricing methodology for fuel (legal decree, formula components). Documents implementation gaps: Sembrando Vida's land-ownership requirement likely excludes the poorest; scale ~0.3% of GDP — qualification and limitation findings. Price-guarantee and fertilizer program scaling (five states to nine) — execution finding. Retailer price-cap agreement for 24 goods — policy action finding. |
| **Adjacent context** | None required; effectiveness data, methodology, and implementation qualification findings independently meet the evidence test. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0076 — page 76 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.1, 5B.10 |
| **Lenses cited** | 1, 10 |
| **Relevance** | Quantifies economic integration and trajectory change over time: manufacturing sector now ~50% domestic value-added driven by foreign demand; automotive 80%. Remittances increased from <1% of GDP (2000) to ~4% (2021). Regression coefficient of U.S. GDP impact on Mexico GDP rose from ~0.2% (1980s) to 1.5% (2010s) — measured outcome of NAFTA-era integration trajectory. Manufacturing sector explains ~75% of Mexico's short-term GDP fluctuations despite being only ~20% of GDP. Documents structural economic trajectory inherited and the transmission channel — material to 5B.10's "stronger and more durable economic trajectory than inherited" assessment. |
| **Adjacent context** | Paragraph 1 (NAFTA context) is identifying context, but paragraphs 1–2 independently meet the evidence test with quantified findings and regression results. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0077 — page 77 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.8, 5B.10 |
| **Lenses cited** | 8, 10 |
| **Relevance** | Documents countercyclical nature of remittances (increased during GFC and COVID-19) and near-zero correlation of portfolio flows with business fluctuations. This constitutes a measured distributional buffer outcome and an institutional resilience finding relevant to Mexico's economic trajectory under external shocks — directly material to 5B.10 and partially to 5B.8's distributional incidence across groups. |
| **Adjacent context** | U0076 is necessary adjacent context establishing that remittances now constitute ~4% of GDP; without that scale, the countercyclical buffer finding in U0077 is less interpretable. However, U0076 independently meets the evidence test and is included separately. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0078 — page 78 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.1, 5B.4, 5B.10 |
| **Lenses cited** | 1, 4, 10 |
| **Relevance** | Event-study finding: 2014 U.S. sanctions on Russia associated with USD 0.85 billion (~0.07 pp of 2012 GDP) increase in Mexico's exports to the U.S. Regression and local projection results showing statistically significant ~10% nominal export increase at four-month lag. Documents a measured trade diversion effect — evidence of how Mexico's export regime performed under an external shock, relevant to both trajectory (5B.10) and trade/investment framework (5B.4). |
| **Adjacent context** | Annex intro and paragraph 1 (sanctions context) are identifying context only. The empirical estimates in paragraphs 2–3 independently meet the evidence test. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0079 — page 79 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.1, 5B.4, 5B.10 |
| **Lenses cited** | 1, 4, 10 |
| **Relevance** | Contains the methodology caveat for U0078's sanctions analysis: regression approaches may capture time-varying effects other than sanctions; local projections using separate executive-order months partially mitigate. Also contains the completed impulse response description. This is a contrary/methodological qualification finding that could merit a distinct evidence record — it qualifies the causal claim from U0078 and should be attributed alongside U0078's findings. |
| **Adjacent context** | U0078 is necessary to interpret this qualification; U0078 is already included on its own evidence. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |

---

### U0080 — page 80 — **INCLUDE**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Question IDs** | 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| **Lenses cited** | 3, 8, 9 |
| **Relevance** | Quantified inflation comparison finding: food prices contributed roughly half of the increase in inflation above Banxico's upper target limit — a specific distributional composition finding. Documents forecast error (actual vs. in-sample Phillip-curve forecast) — evidence-quality finding relevant to 5B.7's independent evaluation permit question. Documents historical pattern: food price inflation above target for a year or more in 2008, 2011–13, 2017–18 — temporal fit evidence for 5B.10. |
| **Adjacent context** | U0073 and U0074 provide the 2022 policy response context; U0080 focuses on the inflation diagnosis (food contribution) and forecast performance, which independently meet the evidence test. |
| **Exclusion reason** | N/A — chunk is included. |
